name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail lost in upscaling by using depth maps, which directly improves output quality without extra compute cost—just a smarter tool. The trade-off is integration time: we must adapt the node to EXCAVA’s workflow, but the payoff is immediate quality gains with no new model dependencies. Skip the motion-refiner for now; depth-aware upscaling hits harder for EXCAVA’s core task.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t touch EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a spatial fix for a temporal problem. The real risk is wasting integration time on a dead end while motion blur remains the bottleneck. Test the motion-refiner node from SD3.5-Ultra first; if it fails, we’ll know depth-upscaling is the only play left.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner node to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It directly targets motion blur—the biggest visible flaw in EXCAVA’s output—by refining motion vectors in latent space, which no depth-upscaler can fix. The trade-off is one extra pass over the frames, but the quality gain from sharper motion outweighs the minor slowdown. Depth-upscaling can wait until motion blur is resolved; it’s a spatial fix for a temporal problem.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-2778, worker-4124 — done, dissolved]

name: Torque
text: The motion-refiner node is a gamble—SD3.5-Ultra’s 404 errors prove the model’s access is unreliable, so even if it works today, it could break tomorrow. Instead, test a lightweight temporal denoiser (e.g., RVRT or a custom optical flow pass) first—it’s a safer spatial-temporal fix with no model dependency. Settle it by running both on a 10-frame burst: if the denoiser drops motion blur by 0.5% with zero risk of failure, it wins.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Skip both SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner and InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-up; test RVRT temporal denoiser first—it’s a safer spatial-temporal fix with no model dependency. Gearbox owns the integration and must deliver a working RVRT node in EXCAVA’s pipeline within 48 hours.
